subject: Post-call: ACME Retail evaluation — integration plan & success criteria
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver@acmeretail.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-03 15:20 -0500
Subject: Post-call recap + proposed POC integration plan

Hi Oliver / Priya —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and a concrete next-steps proposal so we can get the evaluation started next week. I tried to capture both the business success criteria ACME mentioned and the minimal integration path so your engineers can validate feasibility quickly.

High-level success criteria (you flagged these as important):
- Latency: 95th percentile generation latency < 600ms for 50–100 token prompts for our core product flows.
- Quality: pass rate >= 90% on the 40-item prompt set (we'll run the shared eval).
- Throughput: sustained 120 req/min across peak hour without error spikes.
- Cost target: unit inference cost target <$0.03 per thousand tokens (goal to compare across model variants).
- Security: data residency in us-east-1 and SOC2 evidence for request logs.

Proposed POC scope & timeline (3 weeks, can compress with committed engineering):
1) Week 0 — Kickoff (this week): finalize SOW and security contacts (legal + infra).
2) Week 1 — Baseline integration (sandbox): SDK install + sample /v1/generate call, baseline latency and correctness tests.
3) Week 2 — Feature integration & streaming: implement streaming responses and tool-calling for the product's external API hooks; integrate KV cache for session-based flows.
4) Week 3 — Evaluation & wrap: run the 40-prompt eval, throughput load test, and present results + next-step recommendation.

Ownership (suggested):
- Redwood integration lead: Sergio Alvarez — technical point for SDK, API routes, streaming, and tool-calls.
- Redwood sales/POC owner: Marissa Cole — coordinates logistics, success criteria sign-off, and procurement.
- ACME technical lead: Oliver Grant — infrastructure/engineering contact for sandbox and production network setup.
- ACME security/compliance: Priya Shah — handle SOC2 evidence and KMS/HSM questions.

Technical integration notes (minimum viable path):
- SDK: Add the Redwood JavaScript SDK (npm package: @redwood/inference) into your service. Quick start code in the attached SOW.
- API routes: initial calls use /v1/generate with model "redwood-small-v1" for baseline. We recommend trying the "redwood-medium-q4f" quantized variant if latency allows.
- Streaming: enable chunked streaming for long responses; SDK exposes a stream() helper and a webhooks fallback.
- Tool calling: a small JSON schema for functions — see sample function signature in the SOW; we support synchronous and async tool calls.
- KV cache: optional prefix caching for repeated prompts; we can show a 2–4x token cost reduction in the demo.

Attachments: redwood-poc-statement-of-work.pdf (SOW + sample code), acme-sample-integration-checklist.xlsx

Next steps I propose:
1) Oliver — confirm acceptance of the timeline and owners by EOD Thursday 2025-11-06.
2) Priya — can your security team send SOC2 contact and any specific evidence requirements?
3) We will schedule a 60-minute tech kickoff with Sergio + ACME engineers; proposed slot: Mon 2025-11-10 10:00 AM ET.

I can make the kickoff earlier if you want to accelerate.

Thanks — Jordan

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + proposed POC integration plan

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap. This aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side before we lock dates: 

1) Latency target — the 600ms 95th is tight for us; it's a target but we need to understand sample payload sizes. Our average prompt is ~85 tokens with a 40-token expected response. Will that fit your baseline model selection?
2) Streaming — we need a server-side event approach (SSE) that works with our load balancer. Any past customers using SSE at scale?
3) Security — Priya will send the list of artifacts we need. For KMS we use AWS KMS (alias/acme-prod).
4) Network — we need to run the sandbox within our VPC and connect via an outbound NAT; is Private deployment required or will Dedicated suffice for the trial?

We'll confirm the tech kickoff slot once Priya and Kunal check calendars. Also, we need a short statement of work for procurement — can Marissa share a one-page summary she can present to procurement?

Oliver
VP, Engineering — ACME Retail

Oliver — quick answers inline and a small update to the plan.

1) Latency & models: the baseline model "redwood-small-v1" should meet the latency target for the prompt size you shared. We will run an initial calibration test during Week 1 and, if needed, recommend the quantized medium variant. We'll include sample payloads in the kickoff doc.
2) Streaming & SSE: we support SSE and native WebSocket streaming via the SDK. Several retail customers use SSE behind LB — I’ll have Sergio send a short note with the deployment pattern we recommend (keep-alive, chunk sizes).
3) Security & KMS: Private deployment is not required for the sandbox. Dedicated capacity in us-east-1 with customer-managed VPC peering is the pragmatic middle ground for evaluation; Priya can confirm. Marissa will attach the procurement one-pager.

Updated timeline: we can shift Week 1 to include an initial calibration run (2–4 hours) so you have concrete numbers before committing to model variants.

Thanks — Jordan

Subject: Technical kickoff checklist & SSE deployment notes

Oliver / team — per Jordan's ask, here's a compact checklist I will walk through during the kickoff. I'll also paste the recommended SSE pattern below so your infra can pre-check it.

Kickoff checklist (30–60 min):
- Introductions & owners (5 min)
- Sandbox & credentials: confirm sandbox VPC access, outbound NAT, and IP allowlists (5 min)
- Quick SDK demo: npm install & /v1/generate smoke test (10 min)
- Streaming demo: SSE example + fallbacks (10 min)
- Tool calling & function schema: show sample function call and response handling (10 min)
- Next steps & load-test schedule (5 min)

SSE deployment pattern (recommendation):
- Use chunked SSE endpoint exposed by the SDK (path: /v1/stream).
- Keep idle-timeout > 120s on LB. Use ping heartbeats every 20s.
- Recommended chunk size: 512–2048 bytes depending on your response shape.
- Fallback: if SSE blocked, use long-polling with incremental checkpoints.

API & SDK notes (implementation specifics):
- Auth: Bearer token via Authorization header; tokens tied to sandbox capacity.
- Endpoints: /v1/generate (sync), /v1/stream (SSE/WebSocket streaming), /v1/function_call (tool-calling helper with idempotency-token).
- Tool schema example: {"name":"lookupCustomer","params":{"customer_id":"string"}} — SDK will surface typed helpers.
- KV cache: recommend local LRU 10k entries for session reuse, plus a small TTL (5–10m) to avoid stale outputs.

Acceptance test plan (brief):
- Calibration run: 100 sample prompts (mix of short and medium) to measure 95th percentile latencies.
- Functional eval: run the shared 40-prompt set; target >= 90% pass.
- Load test: ramp to 2x your expected peak for 10 minutes to validate autoscaling and error behavior.

I'll bring a short README and the sample code to the kickoff. If there are specific payloads you want us to include in the calibration run, please drop them into the Drive link above.

See you at the kickoff — Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
